title: Vendor Relationship
description: Structural relationship between the seller reporting a vendor-defined metric and the `vendor` that produced it — *who* measured, relative to the seller, not *how* and not *how well*. This is a relationship disposition, NOT a trust ranking: `third_party` is not "more trustworthy" than `first_party` — an issuer-paid vendor on a terminable contract is not automatically more independent than an attested, recomputable first-party measurement. Trust and quality questions belong to the vendor catalog's `accreditations[]`, `standard_reference`, `methodology_url` / `methodology_version`, and to any future confidence or attestation surface (#5758), not to this enum. Every value is defined on checkable structural facts (ownership, control, corporate identity) so the field stays coarse and verifiable; methodology (instrument, model, panel, sensor) is an open corpus and lives at the vendor's measurement-agent catalog (`get_adcp_capabilities.measurement.metrics[]`). The relationship is a property of the (seller, vendor) pair, not of the vendor: the same measurement agent is `first_party` when its operator sells the inventory and `third_party` when an unrelated seller reports the same metric. Declared by the seller on `reporting_capabilities.vendor_metrics[]` — REQUIRED whenever `vendor` resolves to the seller's own `brand.json` or to an entity under common ownership or control with the seller — and MAY be echoed on `vendor_metric_values[]` rows so a delivery report is self-describing without a discovery hop. Absence means *undeclared*; it MUST NOT be read as `third_party`. Generalises the `completion_source` pattern (`seller_attested` / `vendor_attested`) from `completion_rate` to every vendor metric. Distinct from `delivery-metrics.json#/properties/measurement_source`, which names the audience-measurement provider (`nielsen_audio`, `geopath`) behind a measured-channel row.

enumDescriptions.first_party: The seller (or the seller's own measurement agent) produced the number: `vendor` resolves to the selling party's own `brand.json`. Covers seller-operated sensors (DOOH camera or WiFi presence, in-store retail-media counting, cinema audience counting), walled-garden self-reported measurement, and retail-media closed loops. The seller MUST still publish the metric in a `brand.json` `agents[type='measurement']` catalog like any other vendor; `first_party` is a disclosure, not an exemption from the catalog contract.
enumDescriptions.affiliated: The vendor is a distinct legal entity under common ownership or control with the seller — a parent or subsidiary, a controlling or majority equity stake, a joint venture, or disclosed board overlap. Defined on structural facts only: a commercial dependency (an issuer-pays vendor whose principal customer is the seller) does NOT make a vendor `affiliated`, however real the incentive problem — that concern is graded, not binary, and belongs to accreditation, methodology, and confidence surfaces (#5758) rather than to this enum. Buyers MAY treat `affiliated` as `first_party` for reconciliation purposes; if the set is ever collapsed to two values it collapses toward `first_party`, never toward `third_party`.
enumDescriptions.third_party: An independent measurement vendor with no ownership or control relationship to the seller (Nielsen, DoubleVerify, IAS, Adelaide, Lumen, TVision, Scope3, Kantar, etc.). Source of truth is the vendor. This is the topology the `vendor_metric` surface was designed around. It is a structural fact, not a quality grade — see the type description — and it is never the default: a seller that omits the field has declared nothing.
